sections.h2: Where does a deed get recorded in Trumbull County, Ohio?
sections.html:
Deeds for land anywhere in Trumbull County are recorded at the Recorder's Office, 160 High Street NW, Warren, Ohio 44481. The office is open weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and it stops taking documents at 4:00 p.m. so staff can balance the day's transactions.

The recorder's own description of the job is to record, file and index papers that touch real estate, including deeds, mortgages, easements, leases, powers of attorney, plats and mechanic's liens. Records are indexed by name, not by street address, so a search for one owner will list every parcel that person holds. The county has images and data online for every record except military discharges, reaching back to 1795, the year of the first recordings in the county.

A seller does not usually deal with the recorder directly. The closing agent or title company hands the deed through the tax map office and the auditor first, then files it here. Knowing the sequence helps when a closing date is tight.

sections.h2: What does the Trumbull County Recorder charge to record a deed?
sections.html:
Since April 1, 2025, the recorder has charged $39 for the first two pages of most documents and $8 for each page after that. The increase of $5 came from Senate Bill 94, which allows a preservation surcharge on top of the base fees in Ohio Revised Code 317.32. The recorder's fee page prints a sample chart:

Trumbull County Recorder fees printed on the county fee schedule
ItemFee
1 or 2 pages$39
3 pages$47
5 pages$63
10 pages$103
Marginal reference on a separate instrument$4 each
Document that misses layout standards$20 extra

Source: Trumbull County Recorder fee schedule.

Other charges from the same schedule and the recorder's FAQ:

  • Certified copy: $2 a page, plus $1 for the seal.
  • Copies made with staff help: $2 a page.
  • Plats: ten cents per square inch, with a $40 minimum.
  • Military records: no fee.
  • Cards: a 2.60 percent convenience fee applies to debit and credit payments.

Cash, checks, money orders and e-checks are also accepted. By mail, an underpayment or overpayment sends the package back unrecorded, and the office will not mail cash back, so send a check or money order.

sections.h2: Which layout rules can add $20 to a Trumbull County recording?
sections.html:
Any document that falls short of the state formatting standard is recorded with a $20 surcharge, and the same charge applies automatically to e-filed documents that miss the mark. The recorder posts the checklist on its requirements page.

  • Type of 10 point or larger.
  • Paper from 8 1/2 by 11 inches up to 8 1/2 by 14.
  • Black or blue ink only, with no highlighting.
  • A 3 inch blank band at the top of page one for the recorder, auditor and engineer.
  • A 1 1/2 inch margin at the top of later pages, and 1 inch on the sides and bottom.
  • Legible notary stamps and signatures in black or blue ink, with a printed name under any signature that is hard to read.
  • A line near the end stating who prepared the instrument.

Court and tax authority papers, plats, DD214 discharges, state and federal documents and anything signed before July 1, 2009 are exempt from the standard.

sections.h2: How does a deed move through the Trumbull County offices?
sections.html:
A deed cannot go straight to the recorder. The county auditor's conveyance page says a deed filing must carry the required forms and a legible copy of the last deed of record, and it goes first to the Tax Map Office, then to the Auditor, and last to the Recorder. The Auditor sits on the second floor of the Administration Building and can be reached at 330-675-2420; the tax map department's number is 330-675-2473.

  • The Tax Map Office reviews the legal description and parcel split, if any.
  • The Auditor collects the conveyance fee and stamps the deed. The county prices it at $4.00 per thousand dollars of value conveyed plus $0.50 per parcel, and an exempt transfer costs only the $0.50 per parcel.
  • The Recorder files and indexes the deed after that.

Two checks are needed: one to the Auditor for conveyance fees, a second to the Recorder for recording. Mailed transfers are accepted at the 160 High Street NW address with a stamped return envelope, and the Auditor posts conveyance standards written with the county engineer. Ohio also lets a county levy its own transfer tax of up to thirty cents per hundred dollars under section 322.02, so ask the auditor which charges apply to your deed.

The recorder tries to send originals back within 24 business hours, and most filings go out the same day. Deeds that must pass through other offices first can take longer. The office also takes eRecording through four partner vendors and accepts most documents, transfer documents included.

sections.h2: What will the Trumbull County Recorder not do for a seller?
sections.html:
State law bars recorder staff from running title searches, so the office cannot tell you whether a parcel is clear. Employees also cannot draft or notarize a deed, choose a form or advise on one, and the office sells no blank forms. Attorneys and title companies handle those jobs.

The FAQ offers a few points worth knowing before listing a house:

  • A deed is binding even when unrecorded, but recording protects the new owner, because the public record would otherwise still show the former owner holding title and able to borrow against it.
  • A recorded deed cannot be edited. Adding or removing a name takes a new deed, and a mistake should go to an attorney.
  • A deed covers the land, so building a house later does not produce a new deed.
  • Re-recording is allowed only when the document itself states the reason, and costs the standard fee plus $4.

Torrens (registered land) filings were taken through June 1996 and are no longer accepted.

sections.h2: How are mortgage releases and liens handled in Trumbull County?
sections.html:
A mortgage is released when the lender records a satisfaction. The lender starts that step, and some send the paper to the borrower, who can then bring the original to the recorder with the fee and a stamped return envelope. After a payoff, call the lender to ask how the release will be filed, then confirm with the recorder that it was recorded.

Only the party that filed a lien can remove it, and the recorder does not report liens to credit bureaus or notify them when one is released. Mechanic's liens can be checked in the recorder's search, but judgment and other liens may sit with the Clerk of Courts or at the state level, which is why the recorder suggests hiring a title examiner. Deed restrictions and oil and gas interests also need an examiner's review.

sections.h2: What does Trumbull County look like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Trumbull County is in the far northeast corner of Ohio, with Warren as county seat and largest city. It was organized on July 10, 1800 and named for the Connecticut governor Jonathan Trumbull, because the land came out of the Connecticut Western Reserve. At 637 square miles it is described by Wikipedia as roughly square, the only square county in Ohio. Cities include Cortland, Girard, Hubbard, Niles and Warren, with villages such as Lordstown and Newton Falls. Interstate 80 and US 422 cross the county.

The Census Bureau reports these figures:

  • Estimated population in 2025: 198,972, compared with 201,977 in the 2020 count.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes, 2020 to 2024: $141,800.
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 71.3 percent across 86,550 households.
  • Median gross rent: $797 a month.
  • Median household income: $56,435.
  • Share of residents age 65 or older: 24.3 percent.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 112.

Before you list, pull together the last recorded deed and any lien releases, so the tax map office and auditor can process the transfer without a second trip.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Trumbull County?
faqs.a: The county charges $39 for a deed of one or two pages and $8 for each extra page, plus $4 for each marginal reference. A document that does not meet the layout rules carries an extra $20. The auditor's conveyance fee is separate and is paid by check to the Auditor.

faqs.q: Does Trumbull County record deeds by mail?
faqs.a: Yes. Include the deed that has passed the tax map office and the Auditor, a check in the exact amount, and a self-addressed stamped envelope. Packages with the wrong amount are returned unrecorded, and the office does not mail back cash.

faqs.q: Can the Trumbull County Recorder do a title search for me?
faqs.a: No. State law prohibits the office from doing real estate title searches. Title companies and attorneys search the records and back the result with title insurance. You can search the county's online index yourself.

faqs.q: How long does Trumbull County take to return a recorded deed?
faqs.a: Most documents go out the same day. The recorder aims to return originals within 24 business hours, and deeds that must clear other offices first may take a little longer. Originals go back to whoever submitted them.

faqs.q: Is a deed valid if I never record it in Trumbull County?
faqs.a: A deed binds the parties even when unrecorded, but the recorder advises recording it. Until it is on record, the public index still shows the former owner, who could take out a mortgage or have a judgment attach to the property.
